title: Coherent scalar extension for exterior powers, duals and determinant wedges
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $V$ a direct summand of a finite free $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. For $r\ge0$, using exterior powers [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra] and ordinary module tensor [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], the maps
$$B\otimes_A\bigwedge_A^rV\longrightarrow\bigwedge_B^r(B\otimes_AV),\quad b\otimes(v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_r)\longmapsto b((1\otimes v_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge(1\otimes v_r)),$$
$$B\otimes_A V^\vee\longrightarrow(B\otimes_AV)^\vee,\quad b\otimes\lambda\longmapsto\bigl(b'\otimes v\longmapsto bb'\lambda(v)\bigr),\qquad V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A(V,A),$$
are isomorphisms, natural in $V$; the dual map is natural for the contravariant dual action. They commute with evaluation, ordinary tensor symmetry, and the identity and associativity identifications of scalar extension. For the variable-rank determinant modules [def-trf-projective-determinant-module], the top exterior comparisons induce an isomorphism $s_V:B\otimes_A\det_A(V)\cong\det_B(B\otimes_AV)$, natural for isomorphisms of finite projective modules, including the unit comparison for $V=0$. For every short exact sequence $0\to U\to V\to W\to0$ of finite projective $A$-modules, the scalar extension of its kernel-first wedge map $\gamma:\det_A(U)\otimes_A\det_A(W)\cong\det_A(V)$ [lem-trf-projective-determinant-exact-sequence] agrees, via these comparisons, with the kernel-first wedge map of the scalar-extended sequence. No flatness hypothesis on $B$ is imposed.

proof.text:
Write $\alpha:A\to B$. Tensor balancing gives the comparison
$B\otimes_A(M\otimes_AN)\cong(B\otimes_AM)\otimes_B(B\otimes_AN)$ by $b\otimes(m\otimes n)\mapsto(b\otimes m)\otimes(1\otimes n)$, with inverse $(b\otimes m)\otimes(c\otimes n)\mapsto bc\otimes(m\otimes n)$. Units, symmetry and successive scalar extension are given respectively by multiplication, interchange of the module entries, and $c\otimes(b\otimes m)\mapsto c\beta(b)\otimes m$ for $B\xrightarrow{\beta}C$. Each inverse and each constraint equation follows by substitution on pure tensors, which span. Tensoring a retract $V\xrightarrow{i}A^n\xrightarrow{p}V$, $pi=1$, remains a retract since $(1\otimes p)(1\otimes i)=1$; the explicit coordinate maps identify $B\otimes_AA^n$ with $B^n$. Thus $V_B$ is finite projective, without any flatness assumption.

source.place: Tag 00DM (section-tensor-algebra), tensor conventions; explicit balanced-map argument for scalar constraints and preservation of a finite-free retract.

proof.text:
The same retract supplies a finite dual frame: put $v_j=p(e_j)$ and $\lambda_j=e_j^*i$, so $v=\sum_j\lambda_j(v)v_j$. Consequently every $\lambda\in V^\vee$ satisfies $\lambda=\sum_j\lambda(v_j)\lambda_j$. Define $d_V(b\otimes\lambda)(c\otimes v)=bc\alpha(\lambda(v))$; both tensor relations and $B$-linearity follow from this formula. An inverse is
$h\longmapsto\sum_j h(1\otimes v_j)\otimes\lambda_j$.
Indeed $d_V$ of this sum, evaluated at $c\otimes v$, is $c\sum_jh(1\otimes v_j)\alpha(\lambda_j(v))=h(c\otimes v)$. Conversely the inverse applied to $d_V(b\otimes\lambda)$ is $\sum_jb\alpha(\lambda(v_j))\otimes\lambda_j=b\otimes\lambda$. These calculations establish invertibility and show that the inverse does not depend on the retract.

source.place: Tag 00NX (lemma-finite-projective), finite-free retract characterization; explicit finite-frame calculation filling the dual scalar comparison.

proof.text:
By the exterior universal property, the alternating map $(v_j)\mapsto(1\otimes v_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge(1\otimes v_r)$ induces, after tensor balancing, the stated $B$-linear map $c_{r,V}$. To construct its inverse, extend the formula
$((b_1\otimes v_1),\ldots,(b_r\otimes v_r))\mapsto(\prod_jb_j)\otimes(v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_r)$
additively in each entry. Replacing $b_j\alpha(a)\otimes v_j$ by $b_j\otimes av_j$ leaves this value unchanged, so repeated tensor universality makes it a $B$-multilinear map on $V_B^r$. It is alternating: when two arguments equal $\sum_k b_k\otimes v_k$, the terms with the same summand twice vanish and the terms indexed by $(k,l)$ and $(l,k)$ cancel by $v_k\wedge v_l=-v_l\wedge v_k$. This uses alternation, not division by $2$. The universal property over $B$ now gives a map from $\bigwedge_B^rV_B$. Both composites are the identity on pure wedges by the displayed formulas, hence on their spans. For $r=0$ these maps are multiplication $B\otimes_AA\cong B$ and its inverse. This construction in fact works for every $A$-module.

source.place: Tag 00DM (section-tensor-algebra), alternating quotient; explicit scalar-extension construction from the universal property.

proof.text: For an $A$-linear map $f:V\to W$, both exterior naturality composites send $b\otimes(v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_r)$ to $b\bigwedge_j(1\otimes f(v_j))$. For $\mu\in W^\vee$, both sides of $d_V(1\otimes f^\vee)=f_B^\vee d_W$ evaluated on $c\otimes v$ give $bc\alpha(\mu(f(v)))$. Evaluation after scalar extension and evaluation after $d_V$ likewise both give $bc\alpha(\lambda(v))$; interchanging tensor factors changes $bc$ to $cb$, which is equal. Exterior products commute with $c$ because concatenating the two wedge tuples before or after applying $c$ gives the same wedge, with the same scalar product. Under $A\to B\xrightarrow{\beta}C$, the two exterior maps on $c\otimes(b\otimes\bigwedge_jv_j)$ both give $c\beta(b)\bigwedge_j(1\otimes v_j)$. The two dual maps evaluated on $t\otimes v$ both give $ct\beta(b)\beta\alpha(\lambda(v))$. For identity scalar extension the formulas reduce to multiplication by the original scalars. Spanning pure tensors and wedges proves all these equations and compatibility with the ordinary tensor associators and symmetry of step 1.

source.place: Tag 00DM (section-tensor-algebra); generator calculations for exterior and dual naturality, products, evaluation, symmetry, units and scalar towers.

proof.text: Taking all degrees together, the maps $c_{r,V}$ give a multiplicative map of exterior algebras, by the product calculation in step 4. Define a map $s_V:B\otimes_AD_A(V)\to D_B(V_B)$ by $b\otimes x\mapsto b\,\bigwedge(v\mapsto1\otimes v)(x)$. For $x\in D_A(V)$ its image wedges to zero with $1\otimes v$ for every $v$, since it is the image of $x\wedge v=0$. Every element of $V_B$ is a sum of $c\otimes v$, so it wedges to zero with every element of $V_B$. This proves that the formula lands in the socle and is balanced. No assertion that tensoring preserves annihilators has been used; invertibility will be proved on charts.

source.place: Tag 0FJA (remark-determinant-as-socle); explicit restriction of the multiplicative exterior scalar map to the socle.

proof.text:
Choose a finite standard free cover $A_{f_a}$ for $V$; the images $g_a=\alpha(f_a)$ generate $1$ in $B$. Tensor balancing identifies $(V_B)_{g_a}$ with $B_{g_a}\otimes_{A_{f_a}}V_{f_a}$, so it is free on the extended basis. Chart descent identifies $D_A(V)_{f_a}$ and $D_B(V_B)_{g_a}$ with the respective top exterior powers, including zero charts. The tensor identification for the source is explicit:
$(B\otimes_AD_A(V))_{g_a}\cong B_{g_a}\otimes_{A_{f_a}}D_A(V)_{f_a}$,
$(b\otimes x)/g_a^k\mapsto(b/g_a^k)\otimes(x/1)$, with inverse $(b/g_a^k)\otimes(x/f_a^l)\mapsto(b\otimes x)/g_a^{k+l}$.
The localized $s_V$ is the top-degree map of step 3, by its wedge formula, hence an isomorphism. Here the localizations of the socles are supplied by chart descent, rather than by tensor exactness. To obtain a global inverse, let $y\in D_B(V_B)$ and apply the local inverses to $y/1$. On overlaps they agree, since each is inverse to the same localized $s_V$. Module cover exactness glues these to a unique $x\in B\otimes_AD_A(V)$. Uniqueness makes $y\mapsto x$ $B$-linear. Each inverse identity holds locally, and the injectivity clause of module cover exactness makes it hold globally. Thus $s_V$ is the required isomorphism.

proof.text: For an isomorphism $f:V\cong W$, the exterior algebra map carries the socle of $V$ to that of $W$: every $w$ is $f(v)$, so the annihilation equation is preserved. Exterior naturality from step 4 therefore restricts to naturality of $s$. The exterior identity and scalar-tower equations restrict in the same way, so the determinant comparisons obey the identity and associativity constraints. For $V=0$, chart descent identifies both determinant modules with their rings by the empty wedge; the map $s_0$ is $b\otimes a\mapsto b\alpha(a)$. This proves the unit normalization, also for the zero ring and for rings on which the ranks vary.

source.place: Tags 0FJA (remark-determinant-as-socle) and 0FJ9 (section-determinants); restriction of the already proved generator equations; empty-wedge normalization.

proof.text:
For $0\to U\xrightarrow{i}V\xrightarrow{p}W\to0$, projectivity of $W$ gives a section $t$. The maps $U\oplus W\to V$, $(u,w)\mapsto i(u)+t(w)$, and $v\mapsto(u,pv)$ with $i(u)=v-t(pv)$ are inverse. Tensoring their inverse equations shows that the extended sequence is split exact; its three terms are finite projective by step 1. Choose a simultaneous standard free cover for $U,W$ by multiplying members of their finite free covers; these products generate $1$ and the split isomorphism also makes $V$ free there. On such a chart choose bases $u_1,\ldots,u_r$, $w_1,\ldots,w_s$ and lifts $t(w_j)$. The determinant exact-sequence formula before and after scalar extension, and the maps $s$, both send the tensor of their top wedges to
$(1\otimes i(u_1))\wedge\cdots\wedge(1\otimes i(u_r))\wedge(1\otimes t(w_1))\wedge\cdots\wedge(1\otimes t(w_s))$.
An arbitrary scalar multiplies this expression on both sides; these pure wedge tensors span the chart source. Thus the square with $B\otimes_A\gamma_{i,p}$, $s_U\otimes s_W$ (using step 1), $s_V$, and $\gamma_{i_B,p_B}$ commutes locally. The equality-detection clause of module cover exactness, applied to the difference at each source element, makes it commute globally. Empty basis lists give exactly the same argument when either rank is zero. No tensor preservation of a nonsplit exact sequence is invoked.
